item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material workflow-experience decisions remain unresolved: the Work entry experience, workflow-change activation, and operator-visible provider failover.","questions":[{"decision_key":"work_new_conversation_entry","label":"Work entry experience","context":"The new Work tab must support Chat, Coding, and Research without making the operator navigate through unnecessary setup. A hero control is a primary action visible immediately; advanced controls are secondary settings,[F","evidence":"`apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently exposes the five-tab Lab/Router/Models/Review/Settings shell, while the verified six-tab decision replaces Lab with a Work surface containing explicit Chat, Coding, and Research modes. No current surface establishes how a new conversation begins.","impact":"This determines the Work tab’s first screen, how quickly operators can start, and whether mode-specific requirements remain understandable as Work gains more capabilities.","question":"What should an operator see first when starting a new Work conversation?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Mode-aware composer","consequence":"Show one composer immediately with Chat, Coding, and Research selectors; changing mode reveals only required inputs such as a coding workspace or research source policy. This is fast now and preserves explicit mode contracts long term, but the composer must adapt clearly."},{"number":2,"text":"Choose mode first","consequence":"Require a Chat, Coding, or Research choice before showing the composer. This makes each flow unambiguous, but adds a step to every new conversation and may feel slow for frequent operators."},{"number":3,"text":"Unified automatic composer","consequence":"Start from one generic prompt and infer the mode. This minimizes initial UI, but makes workspace, validation, and source-policy behavior less predictable and creates hidden routing rules long term."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A mode-aware composer keeps the three explicit Work contracts visible while preserving a one-screen start and providing room for mode-specific safety inputs.","priority":88},{"decision_key":"published_workflow_edit_activation","label":"Workflow edit activation","context":"A published workflow is the version eligible to start scheduled, batch, or manual runs. The unresolved decision is whether editing that definition changes future execution immediately or produces a separate version.","evidence":"`services/nexus-node/src/nexus-node.mjs` is the durable authority that continues accepted work after clients close, and `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines immutable run states. The verified architecture assigns schedules, batches, and stage definitions to Workflows, but it does not specify when edits to an active definition become executable.","impact":"This changes the Workflows tab’s save and publish controls now, and determines whether future runs remain reproducible against a stable definition as collaboration and scheduling expand.","question":"When an operator edits a published workflow, when should the changes become eligible for new runs?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Draft then publish","consequence":"Every edit creates a draft version; existing schedules keep using the published version until explicit validation and publish. This adds a deliberate release step but gives reproducible runs and safe collaboration."},{"number":2,"text":"Scheduled activation","consequence":"Edits create a version that activates at a chosen time after validation. This supports coordinated operations but adds timing, cancellation, and timezone complexity to the first production release."},{"number":3,"text":"Immediate activation","consequence":"Saving changes updates all future starts immediately while running work stays pinned. This is simplest for rapid iteration but makes accidental changes more likely and weakens operational review."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Draft-then-publish aligns durable scheduled execution with immutable evidence: every run can identify the reviewed workflow version that produced it.","priority":94},{"decision_key":"automatic_provider_failover_visibility","label":"Failover visibility","context":"Provider failover means an unsuccessful model endpoint returns an error and NexusCentral automatically tries the next eligible item in its named queue group. The decision here is how prominently that automatic attempt-by" ,"evidence":"`kits/routing-kit/index.mjs` already owns candidate rationale, fallback, and route lifecycle, while `kits/jobs-kit/index.mjs` owns progress and terminal state. The recorded provider decision requires endpoint failure to route automatically to the next queue object, but the operator experience for that attempt chain is unspecified.","impact":"This determines the live status shown in Workflows and Runs, how operators distinguish ordinary recovery from degradation, and whether the system remains understandable as provider meshes grow.","question":"How should automatic provider failover appear during and after a run?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Summary with expandable attempts","consequence":"Show current provider, failover count, and final outcome by default, with an expandable timestamped attempt chain and errors. This keeps the hero view calm while preserving durable operational evidence."},{"number":2,"text":"Every attempt inline","consequence":"Stream each provider selection, error, and retry in the primary run view. This maximizes immediate transparency but can overwhelm routine work and make healthy recovery look alarming."},{"number":3,"text":"Final route only","consequence":"Show only the provider that completed or the final exhaustion error, leaving intermediate attempts in diagnostics. This is visually simple but hides degradation patterns and slows operator investigation."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A concise summary plus expandable evidence matches the technical-operator audience without letting normal failover noise dominate the primary workflow.","priority":86}]}
